title: Operating systems
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand how operating systems manage hardware for programs: processes and the kernel, the process API, CPU scheduling, threads, locks, condition variables and semaphores, classic concurrency problems and deadlock, address spaces, paging and virtual memory, file systems and storage, crash consistency, protection and virtualization.
primary_reading: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (free textbook)

weeks.1: What an operating system does: processes and the kernel
weeks.2: The process API: fork, exec and wait
weeks.10: Virtual memory: TLBs and page replacement

blocks.deliverable: Trace the process trees of fork programs.
Simulate FIFO, SJF, round robin and MLFQ on a workload.
Week 7 midterm; solve the producer–consumer problem correctly.
Translate addresses and simulate LRU and FIFO replacement.
Trace the disk operations for creating a file.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Write simulators in Python for a CPU scheduler and for a virtual-memory system with page replacement, run them on supplied workloads, and write a report comparing the policies with measured results.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
